chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, does the Tashahhud that is in the second [rak'ah] suffice if I say it in the fourth?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدُ: The Tashahhud, the testimony of faith recited during prayer
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be your ransom (a phrase of respect and devotion)

ai.seo_question: Does a Muslim need to recite the Tashahhud in both the second and fourth rak'ahs of prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the permissibility of omitting the Tashahhud in the final standing position of prayers with more than two rak'ahs, a view that supports the Shia practice of reciting it only once in the second rak'ah. It highlights the flexibility within the ritual structure, distinguishing between the obligatory core of the testimony and the recommended repetitions, thereby simplifying the prayer for the worshiper while maintaining its spiritual essence.
